title: Stinky Bigfoot 'smells like Wasabi' and makes you cry, claims celebrity hunter
excerpt: The mythological beast has eluded thousands of people hell bent on finding it over the years – but now fresh ‘evidence’ has emerged…the Bigfoot’s “horrible” smell

The mythological beast has eluded thousands of people hell bent on finding it over the years – but now fresh ‘evidence’ has emerged…the Bigfoot’s “horrible” smell

14:38, 20 Nov 2026Updated 14:38, 20 Nov 2026

Bigfoot reeks of wasabi and its stench will make you cry, a ‘celebrity’ cryptid hunter has claimed. The mythological beast has eluded thousands of people hell bent on finding it over the years – but now fresh ‘evidence’ has emerged…the Bigfoot’s “horrible” smell.

‌

Article continues below

Speaking to a local news station, South Carolina native Charles ‘Snake’ Stuart claimed he smelt Bigfoot – and it wasn’t pleasant. “These things stink man,” he told WBCD. “I’ve smelt it real up close and it’s like getting smacked in the face with a big thing of wasabi.

‌

“It hit me in the top of the nose – like driving past a dead skunk and you know it clings to your car? It’s like that. It made me cry and vomit.”

‌

He added “there are some sightings [of Bigfoot] in South Carolina – I’ve spoken to a representative there and she says that some people have gone in there and have smelt something absolutely horrible”.

Stuart claims he has spoken to hundreds of people who have also had the grim experience of getting a whiff of the cryptid. “They all say the same thing,” he said. “It smells horrible”.

Earlier in the interview, Stuart says he got his ‘Snake’ moniker after he was “partying” and got a bite from a snake. Stuart says he also has many “concrete” footprints, which he uses as proof that Sasquatch exists.

‌

Earlier this month a spooked motorist called emergency services after an encounter with a towering, sodden creature in the US – just days before a hunter reported being overcome by a foul "smell of death" in the wilderness.

The bizarre encounters were logged by the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization (BFRO), as enthusiasts continue to report sightings despite recent revelations concerning the world's most famous Sasquatch evidence.

Article continues below

The iconic 1967 Patterson-Gimlin tape, long considered the holy grail of Bigfoot sightings, was recently unmasked as a deliberate hoax in filmmaker Marq Evans' documentary Capturing Bigfoot, featuring an admission from Bob Heironimus that he wore the gorilla suit.
